mainTopic: Stories of the חורבן: זכריה's blood, Rome's cruelty, the martyrs, and readings of 'כי עליך הורגנו'
overview: This amud is full of אגדה about the destructions of ירושלים. An old man tells רבי יהושע בן קרחה how נבוזראדן killed huge numbers of people, until their blood reached the boiling blood of the murdered prophet זכריה. The blood rested only when נבוזראדן asked זכריה whether he wanted the whole people destroyed. After that, נבוזראדן repented and became a full גר, and the גמרא lists other enemies whose descendants became Torah scholars. Next the גמרא gives two readings of 'הקול קול יעקב והידים ידי עשו', one about Rome's massacres and one about the power of prayer, and רב teaches that דוד was shown both חורבנות. Then come two stories of martyrs: 400 captive children who drowned themselves rather than sin, and the woman whose seven sons each refused עבודה זרה. Several Sages explain 'כי עליך הורגנו כל היום' in different ways: these martyrs, מילה, scholars who demonstrate שחיטה on themselves, and scholars who give everything for Torah. The amud ends as רבה בר בר חנה begins a new teaching about forty סאה, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The old man's report of the great slaughter
steps.stepSummary: An old man from ירושלים tells רבי יהושע בן קרחה how many people נבוזראדן killed, until their blood touched זכריה's blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבין said in the name of רבי יהושע בן קרחה: An old man from ירושלים told me, 'In this valley נבוזראדן, the captain of the guard, killed 2,110,000 people. In ירושלים he killed 940,000 people on one stone, until their blood flowed and touched the blood of זכריה. This fulfilled the פסוק: "And blood touches blood."'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a story with a reported eyewitness account of how many people נבוזראדן killed. It ends by linking the flowing blood to זכריה's blood and to a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The numbers show how huge the killing was. The key detail is that the blood reached זכריה's blood. That sets up the rest of the story, which explains why זכריה's blood was there at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The Babylonian general who destroyed ירושלים
Captain of the guard (literally: chief of the slaughterers)

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Avin says
that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korḥa says:

phrases.aramaic: סָח לִי זָקֵן אֶחָד מֵאַנְשֵׁי יְרוּשָׁלַיִם:
phrases.english: An old man from the people of Jerusalem told me:

phrases.aramaic: בְּבִקְעָה זוֹ הָרַג נְבוּזַרְאֲדָן רַב טַבָּחִים
phrases.english: In this valley Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, killed
two hundred and eleven times ten thousand (2,110,000),
and in Jerusalem he killed ninety-four times ten thousand (940,000)
on one stone,

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁהָלַךְ דָּמָן וְנָגַע בְּדָמוֹ שֶׁל זְכַרְיָה,
phrases.english: until their blood flowed and touched the blood of Zechariah,
to fulfill what is stated:
"And blood touches blood."
phrases.notes: הושע 4:2

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה, סָח לִי זָקֵן אֶחָד מֵאַנְשֵׁי יְרוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new story
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נבוזראדן's mass killing reached the blood of זכריה, fulfilling the פסוק 'blood touches blood'.
steps.confusionAlert: This זכריה is the כהן and prophet whom the people killed in the בית המקדש (דברי הימים ב 24). He is not the later prophet זכריה whose book is in תרי עשר.

steps.title: נבוזראדן finds the boiling blood and is lied to
steps.stepSummary: נבוזראדן sees blood boiling up from the ground. The people claim it is sacrifice blood, but his test shows it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He found זכריה's blood boiling and rising. He asked, 'What is this?' They told him, 'It is the blood of sacrifices that was spilled.' He brought animal blood to compare, and it did not match.
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes back to explain the details: נבוזראדן finds strange boiling blood and asks about it. The people try to hide the truth, and he catches them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people's excuse is that this is just קרבן blood. נבוזראדן checks the excuse by comparing real animal blood, and it does not match. This sets up his demand for the truth.

phrases.english: He found the blood of Zechariah
that was boiling and rising up,
he said: What is this?
They said to him: It is sacrificial blood that was spilled.
He brought blood, and they were not alike.
phrases.notes: He brought animal blood to compare with the boiling blood, and they looked different.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ לִדְמֵיהּ דִּזְכַרְיָה דַּהֲוָה קָא מִרְתַח וְסָלֵיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the details behind the blood mentioned in Step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The boiling blood was not sacrifice blood, so the people's excuse was false.

steps.title: נבוזראדן threatens them to get the truth
steps.stepSummary: נבוזראדן demands the truth and threatens to torture them if they keep hiding it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: 'If you tell me, good. If not, I will comb your flesh with iron combs.'
steps.whatsHappening: נבוזראדן demands to know whose blood this really is. This step sets up the people's confession in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their lie has failed, so now he forces them with a terrible threat. The question is clear: whose blood is this?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: אִי אָמְרִיתוּ לִי – מוּטָב,
phrases.english: He said to them: If you tell me, good,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָאו – מְסָרֵיקְנָא לְבִשְׂרַיְיכוּ בְּמַסְרְקֵי דְפַרְזְלֵי.
phrases.english: and if not, I will comb your flesh with iron combs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרִיתוּ לִי מוּטָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the lie that was exposed in Step 2
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whose blood is boiling up from the ground?

steps.title: The people confess they killed the prophet
steps.stepSummary: The people admit that the blood belongs to a prophet who rebuked them, whom they murdered. His blood has not rested for many years.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: 'What can we tell you? There was a prophet among us who used to rebuke us about matters of Heaven. We rose up against him and killed him, and for many years now his blood has not rested.'
steps.whatsHappening: The people finally tell the truth: they murdered a prophet, and his blood has been boiling ever since.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answers נבוזראדן's question from Step 3. The blood is not resting because the murder was never set right. That explains the boiling.

phrases.english: They said to him: What shall we tell you?
There was a prophet among us

phrases.aramaic: דַּהֲוָה קָא מוֹכַח לַן בְּמִילֵּי דִשְׁמַיָּא,
phrases.english: who used to rebuke us about heavenly matters,
we rose up against him and killed him,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא כַּמָּה שְׁנִין דְּלָא קָא נָיַיח דְּמֵיהּ.
phrases.english: and for many years now his blood has not settled.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ: מַאי נֵימָא לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the demand of Step 3
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is the blood of a prophet they murdered for rebuking them, and it has not rested for years.

steps.title: נבוזראדן kills group after group, but the blood does not rest
steps.stepSummary: נבוזראדן tries to calm the blood by killing the סנהדרין, then young men and women, then schoolchildren. Each time, the blood still does not settle.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: 'I will appease him.' He brought the Great סנהדרין and a smaller סנהדרין and killed them over the blood, but it did not rest. He killed young men and young women over it, but it did not rest. He brought schoolchildren and killed them over it, but it did not rest.
steps.whatsHappening: נבוזראדן tries to calm זכריה's blood by killing more and more people over it, and none of it works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each group is a step further: the leaders, then the young, then innocent children. The repeated words 'and it did not rest' build tension for the ending.

keyTerms.meaning: The Great סנהדרין (the high court of 71)

phrases.english: He said to them: I will appease him.
He brought the Great Sanhedrin and a lesser Sanhedrin,
killed them over it, and it did not settle.

phrases.aramaic: בַּחוּרִים וּבְתוּלוֹת קְטַל עִילָּוֵיהּ, וְלָא נָח.
phrases.english: Young men and young women he killed over it, and it did not settle.
He brought schoolchildren,
killed them over it, and it did not settle.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: אֲנָא מְפַיֵּיסְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: נבוזראדן reacts to the confession in Step 4
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Killing even the best of the people did not calm זכריה's blood.

steps.title: The blood finally rests
steps.stepSummary: נבוזראדן asks זכריה whether he wants the whole people destroyed. Only then does the blood settle.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'זכריה, זכריה, I have destroyed the best of them. Do you want me to destroy them all?' As soon as he said this, the blood rested.
steps.whatsHappening: נבוזראדן speaks directly to זכריה, and the blood finally settles. The story is not over yet: the next step tells how נבוזראדן reacted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The killing alone did not calm the blood. The blood stopped only when נבוזראדן asked whether זכריה really wanted everyone destroyed. That is the turning point of the story.
steps.whatToRemember: זכריה's blood boiled for years after the people murdered him. נבוזראדן killed the סנהדרין, the young, and the schoolchildren, and none of it calmed the blood. It rested only when he asked if זכריה wanted the whole people destroyed.

phrases.english: He said to him: Zechariah, Zechariah,
the best of them I have destroyed;
would it please you that I destroy them all?
When he said this to him, it settled.

steps.triggerLanguage: זְכַרְיָה, זְכַרְיָה, טוֹבִים שֶׁבָּהֶן אִיבַּדְתִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the failed attempts of Step 5
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: זכריה's blood rested only when נבוזראדן asked if he wanted the entire people destroyed.

steps.title: נבוזראדן repents, flees, and converts
steps.stepSummary: After seeing the blood settle, נבוזראדן reasons with a קל וחומר that his own punishment must be enormous. He runs away, leaves instructions for his property, and converts.
steps.simpleTranslation: At that moment he thought about repenting. He said: 'If this is what happens over one soul, then I, who killed all these souls, deserve much worse!' He ran away, sent a document of instructions to his house, and converted.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with נבוזראדן changing completely. He realizes how guilty he is, leaves his old life, and becomes a גר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reasoning is a simple קל וחומר. The blood of one person, זכריה, did not rest for years and cost many lives, so his own killing of thousands must carry a much heavier punishment. This fear leads him to תשובה and to conversion.

keyTerms.meaning: How much more so, the wording of a קל וחומר
A document spelling out what to do with his property

steps.whatToRemember: The cruel general who destroyed ירושלים ended up repenting and becoming a גר.

phrases.english: At that moment
he thought about repentance in his mind,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר: וּמָה אִם עַל נֶפֶשׁ אַחַת, כָּךְ;
phrases.english: he said: If for one soul, it is like this;
that man who killed
phrases.notes: "That man" is his way of talking about himself.

phrases.english: all of these souls –
how much more so!
He fled, went
and sent a document of instructions to his house,
phrases.notes: It's like a will that says what should happen to everything he owned.

phrases.english: and converted.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּהַהִיא שַׁעְתָּא הַרְהַר תְּשׁוּבָה בְּדַעְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how נבוזראדן responded after the blood finally settled in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נבוזראדן reasoned with a קל וחומר from the punishment for one soul to his own guilt, then repented and converted.

steps.title: נעמן versus נבוזראדן: two kinds of converts
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא contrasts נעמן, who was only a גר תושב, with נבוזראדן, who was a full גר צדק.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: נעמן was a resident non-Jew who kept some laws. נבוזראדן was a full, righteous convert.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא confirming that נבוזראדן's conversion was a complete one, and contrasts him with נעמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גר תושב is a non-Jew who accepts some basic laws but does not become Jewish. A גר צדק fully joins the Jewish people. The ברייתא places נבוזראדן in the higher group, even though נעמן is the more famous non-Jew who recognized ה'.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jew who accepts some basic laws but does not fully convert

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume נעמן converted just because he recognized ה'. The ברייתא says he was only a גר תושב.

phrases.english: It was taught:
Naaman was a resident alien;
phrases.notes: This is the army general of ארם who was healed by אלישע, in מלכים ב פרק ה.

phrases.english: Nebuzaradan was a righteous convert;

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: נַעֲמָן גֵּר תּוֹשָׁב הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports and sharpens the claim in step 7 that נבוזראדן converted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נעמן was a גר תושב, while נבוזראדן was a full גר צדק.

steps.title: Descendants of Israel's enemies who became Torah scholars
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lists descendants of המן, סיסרא and סנחריב who learned and taught תורה, and names שמעיה ואבטליון as descendants of סנחריב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some of המן's descendants studied תורה in בני ברק. Some of סיסרא's descendants taught children in ירושלים. Some of סנחריב's descendants taught תורה in public. Who were they? שמעיה ואבטליון.
steps.whatsHappening: Continuing the theme of enemies whose families joined the Jewish people, the גמרא lists three famous enemies whose descendants became Torah learners and teachers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like נבוזראדן, these were some of Israel's worst enemies. Their descendants still became part of the Torah world. The short question 'Who are they?' points to the most famous example: שמעיה ואבטליון.

keyTerms.meaning: His descendants, literally his children's children

phrases.english: Some of the descendants of Haman
studied Torah in Bnei Brak;
some of the descendants of Sisera
taught children in Jerusalem;
some of the descendants of Sennacherib
taught Torah in public –
Who are they? Shemaya and Avtalyon.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִבְּנֵי בָנָיו שֶׁל הָמָן לִמְּדוּ תּוֹרָה בִּבְנֵי בְרַק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the theme of step 8, enemies who joined the Jewish people, to the descendants of other enemies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Descendants of המן, סיסרא and סנחריב became Torah learners and teachers. The descendants of סנחריב include שמעיה ואבטליון.

steps.title: A פסוק hinting at זכריה's uncovered blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the blood of זכריה and shows that a פסוק in יחזקאל hints at it.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what is written: 'I have set her blood upon the bare rock, so that it should not be covered.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the story of זכריה's boiling blood and connects it to a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes blood left on bare rock so that it cannot be covered. That matches the story, where זכריה's blood stayed out in the open and would not rest for many years. The words הַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב signal that the פסוק fits the story just told.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what is written, linking a story to a פסוק
So that it should not be covered

steps.whatToRemember: The whole story of זכריה's blood is hinted at in יחזקאל: blood on bare rock that is never covered.

phrases.english: This is what is written:
phrases.notes: "This" points back to the story of זכריה's blood.

phrases.english: "I have set her blood upon the bare rock
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 24:8

phrases.english: that it should not be covered."

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side point about converts' descendants and returns to the blood story from steps 4 to 6.
steps.raayaObject: The story that זכריה's blood stayed uncovered and did not rest
steps.raayaSupportSource: יחזקאל 24:8, 'I have set her blood upon the bare rock, that it should not be covered'

steps.title: The voice of יעקב and the hands of עשו: Roman cruelty
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'הקול קול יעקב והידים ידי עשו' is read as describing the massacres of אדריינוס and אספסיינוס and the destruction done by the Roman kingdom.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The voice is the voice of יעקב, and the hands are the hands of עשו.' 'The voice' is אדריינוס קיסר, who killed 600,000 times 600,000 in Alexandria of Egypt, double the number who left Egypt. 'The voice of יעקב' is אספסיינוס קיסר, who killed 4,000,000 in the city of ביתר, and some say 40,000,000. 'The hands are the hands of עשו' is the wicked kingdom that destroyed our houses, burned our היכל, and exiled us from our land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new דרשה on a פסוק from בראשית and uses it to describe the terrible killings and destruction done by Rome.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each part of the פסוק is matched to a different event. 'The voice' is read as the crying of the Jewish people over two huge massacres. 'The hands of עשו' stands for the Roman kingdom itself, which destroyed the בית המקדש and sent us into exile.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sanctuary, the main building of the בית המקדש

phrases.english: 'The voice is the voice of Jacob, and the hands are the hands of Esau':
phrases.notes: בראשית 27:22

phrases.english: 'The voice' is the emperor Hadrian,
who killed in Alexandria of Egypt
six hundred thousand upon six hundred thousand,
double the number of those who left Egypt.
'The voice of Jacob' is the emperor Vespasian,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָרַג בִּכְרַךְ בֵּיתֵּר אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת רִבּוֹא,
phrases.english: who killed four million in the city of Beitar,
and some say: forty million.
'And the hands are the hands of Esau' is the wicked kingdom,
which destroyed our houses,
phrases.notes: Literally 'our houses'; here it means the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: and burned our Sanctuary,
and exiled us from our land.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַקּוֹל קוֹל יַעֲקֹב וְהַיָּדַיִם יְדֵי עֵשָׂו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the blood of זכריה and the first חורבן to the suffering caused by Rome.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק hints at the massacres of אדריינוס and אספסיינוס and at Rome's destruction of the בית המקדש.

steps.title: A second reading: יעקב's prayer and עשו's wars
steps.stepSummary: A second דרשה reads the same פסוק as saying that prayer works through יעקב's children and winning wars works through עשו's children.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: 'The voice is the voice of יעקב' means no prayer succeeds unless some of יעקב's children are part of it. 'And the hands are the hands of עשו' means no war is won unless some of עשו's children are part of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different explanation of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reading made 'voice' mean crying over disasters. This reading makes 'voice' mean prayer, the special strength of יעקב. 'Hands' stands for war, the special strength of עשו.

phrases.english: Another explanation: 'The voice is the voice of Jacob':
there is no prayer that is effective
unless some of the descendants of Jacob are part of it.
'And the hands are the hands of Esau':
there is no war that is victorious
unless some of the descendants of Esau are part of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second reading of the same פסוק explained in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Prayer is the strength of יעקב's children, and war is the strength of עשו's children.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר on the power of the tongue
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says this matches רבי אלעזר's reading of a פסוק in איוב about the tongue.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what רבי אלעזר said: 'You will be hidden from the whip of the tongue' means you will be hidden in the heat of the tongue.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching of רבי אלעזר and says it fits the idea it just taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'והיינו דאמר' tells us that רבי אלעזר's teaching agrees with the idea just taught. He reads 'the scourge of the tongue' in איוב as quarrels stirred up by speech, which a person must hide from.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what he said, meaning it fits what was just taught
Quarrels stirred up by the tongue

phrases.english: And this is what Rabbi Elazar said:
'You shall be hidden from the scourge of the tongue':
phrases.notes: איוב 5:21

phrases.english: you shall hide on account of quarrels stirred up by the tongue.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 12's idea that the voice, meaning speech, is יעקב's power.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that the power of יעקב's children is in their voice.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אלעזר's reading of איוב 5:21 about the tongue.

steps.title: דוד was shown both destructions
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that תהלים 137 shows that הקב״ה showed דוד both the first and the second חורבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: What does the פסוק mean, 'By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat and also cried when we remembered ציון'? It teaches that הקב״ה showed דוד the destruction of the first בית המקדש and of the second. The first one, as it says: 'By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat and also cried.' The second one, as it says: 'Remember, ה׳, against the children of אדום the day of ירושלים, those who said: Tear it down, tear it down, to its very foundation.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב explains a well-known chapter of תהלים. He says that דוד was shown both destructions of the בית המקדש, long before they happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rivers of Babylon point to the first חורבן, done by בבל. The children of אדום point to the second חורבן. This ties back to step 11, where the hands of עשו, the father of אדום, were the Roman kingdom.

keyTerms.meaning: The destruction of the first בית המקדש
The children of אדום, descendants of עשו

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
What is the meaning of what is written:
'By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat,
and also wept, when we remembered Zion'?
phrases.notes: תהלים 137:1

phrases.aramaic: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהֶרְאָהוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְדָוִד
phrases.english: It teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, showed David

phrases.aramaic: חוּרְבַּן בַּיִת רִאשׁוֹן וְחוּרְבַּן בַּיִת שֵׁנִי.
phrases.english: the destruction of the First Temple and the destruction of the Second Temple.
The destruction of the First Temple, as it is stated:

phrases.aramaic: ״עַל נַהֲרוֹת בָּבֶל שָׁם יָשַׁבְנוּ גַּם בָּכִינוּ״.
phrases.english: 'By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat and also wept.'
The Second Temple, as it is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״זְכוֹר ה׳ לִבְנֵי אֱדוֹם אֵת יוֹם יְרוּשָׁלִָים,
phrases.english: 'Remember, O Lord, against the children of Edom the day of Jerusalem,

phrases.aramaic: הָאוֹמְרִים עָרוּ עָרוּ עַד הַיְסוֹד בָּהּ״.
phrases.english: who said: Raze it, raze it, to its very foundation.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 137:7. אדום comes from עשו, whom step 11 tied to the kingdom that destroyed the second בית המקדש.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of the חורבן and ties the second destruction to אדום.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תהלים 137 shows that דוד saw both the first and the second חורבן.

steps.title: The captive children ask about drowning themselves
steps.stepSummary: A story begins about 400 boys and girls taken captive for an immoral purpose. They ask whether they would still have עולם הבא if they drowned themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל, and some say it was רבי אמי, and some say it was taught in a ברייתא: There was a story of 400 boys and girls who were taken captive for shame. They understood what they were wanted for. They said: If we drown ourselves in the sea, will we come to the life of עולם הבא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new, painful story from the time of the חורבן. This step sets up the children's question, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The children would rather die than be forced into sin. What worries them is whether taking their own lives would cost them their share in עולם הבא. The story stops on this question so that an answer can be given.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים, a ברייתא
Taken captive for shame, meaning for immorality
The life of the World to Come

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said,
and some say it was Rabbi Ami,
and some say it was taught in a baraita:
There was an incident with four hundred boys and girls
who were taken captive for shame,
they sensed on their own what they were wanted for,
they said: If we drown in the sea,
will we come to the life of the World to Come?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּאַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת יְלָדִים וִילָדוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story of suffering connected to the חורבן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether drowning themselves to avoid sin would still give them a share in עולם הבא.

steps.title: The oldest child answers from a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The oldest child explains a פסוק in תהלים to show that ה׳ will bring back even those who drown in the sea.
steps.simpleTranslation: The oldest among them taught them: 'ה׳ said: From בשן I will bring back, I will bring back from the depths of the sea.' 'From בשן I will bring back' means from between the teeth of a lion. 'I will bring back from the depths of the sea' means those who drown in the sea.
steps.whatsHappening: The oldest child answers the question with a פסוק. Its message is that those who drown in the sea will be brought back too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads 'בשן' as 'בין שן', between the teeth, as in people killed by a lion. The second half of the פסוק, 'from the depths of the sea', he reads as being about people who drown. This tells the children that they will still have a share in עולם הבא.

phrases.english: The oldest among them expounded to them:
'The Lord said: I will bring back from Bashan,
I will bring back from the depths of the sea':
phrases.notes: תהלים 68:23

phrases.english: 'I will bring back from Bashan': from between the teeth of a lion;
phrases.notes: A play on words: בָּשָׁן is read as בֵּין שֵׁן, 'between the teeth'.

phrases.english: 'I will bring back from the depths of the sea': these are those who drown in the sea.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרַשׁ לָהֶן הַגָּדוֹל שֶׁבָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the children's question from step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. The פסוק promises that ה׳ will bring back those who drown in the sea, so they will come to עולם הבא.

steps.title: The girls and then the boys jump into the sea
steps.stepSummary: After hearing the answer, the girls jump into the sea. The boys use a קל וחומר to reason that they must do the same, and they jump too.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the girls heard this, they all jumped into the sea. The boys reasoned: if the girls, for whom being with men is natural, did this, then we, for whom it is not natural, surely must. So they jumped too.
steps.whatsHappening: The story of the 400 captive children ends. Everyone chooses death in the sea over being used for sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The oldest child's answer, that ה׳ brings back even those who drown, gave them the courage to act. The boys add a קל וחומר. The sin would be worse for them than for the girls, so they have even more reason to refuse it.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'how much more so' argument, reasoning from a lighter case to a stronger one

phrases.english: When the girls heard this,
they all jumped and fell into the sea.
The boys made a 'how much more so' argument about themselves,
and said: If these girls,
whose natural way is for this, acted like this;
phrases.notes: 'For this' means being with men. For the girls that is natural, yet they still chose death over the forced sin.

phrases.english: we, whose natural way is not for this,
how much more so!
They too jumped into the sea.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן שֶׁשָּׁמְעוּ יְלָדוֹת כָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows what the children did after hearing the answer in step 16
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All the children chose death in the sea rather than sin.

steps.title: The verse 'For Your sake we are killed' is about these children
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא connects the children's deaths to the פסוק in תהלים, 'For Your sake we are killed all day.'
steps.simpleTranslation: About them the verse says: 'For Your sake we are killed all day long; we are counted like sheep for slaughter.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the פסוק that describes these children. This also sets up the next step, where רב יהודה gives a different reading of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of people killed for ה׳'s sake. This opinion says it describes the 400 children who died to avoid sin.

keyTerms.meaning: And about them the verse says

steps.whyThisMatters: This פסוק becomes the anchor for the next story. The two opinions disagree about whom it describes.

phrases.english: And about them the verse says:
"For Your sake we are killed all day long,
we are counted like sheep for slaughter."
phrases.notes: תהלים 44:23

steps.triggerLanguage: וַעֲלֵיהֶם הַכָּתוּב אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ties the story in step 17 to a פסוק
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק 'כי עליך הורגנו' refers to the 400 children.

steps.title: רב יהודה: the verse is about the woman and her seven sons; the first son
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says the פסוק is about the woman and her seven sons. The first son refuses idol worship by quoting 'אנכי ה׳ אלהיך' and is killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: This verse is about the woman and her seven sons. They brought the first son before the emperor and told him to worship the idol. He answered that the Torah says, 'I am ה׳ your God.' They took him out and killed him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה offers a different story for the same פסוק and begins telling it, starting with the first son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a second reading of the פסוק from step 18, not a challenge to the story itself. Each son answers the demand by quoting a Torah verse against עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: The woman and her seven sons
They took him out and killed him

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said:
This is the woman and her seven sons.
phrases.notes: He means the same פסוק, 'For Your sake we are killed,' is about them.

phrases.english: They brought the first son
before the emperor,
and they said to him: Worship the idol!
He said to them: It is written in the Torah:
"I am ה׳ your God."
phrases.notes: שמות 20:2

phrases.english: They took him out and killed him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר: זוֹ אִשָּׁה וְשִׁבְעָה בָּנֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different subject for the פסוק quoted in step 18
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב יהודה, the פסוק describes the woman and her seven sons, who were killed for refusing עבודה זרה.

steps.title: The second and third sons refuse and are killed
steps.stepSummary: The second son quotes 'לא יהיה לך אלהים אחרים' and the third quotes 'זובח לאלהים יחרם'. Both are killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: They brought the next son before the emperor and told him to worship the idol. He said the Torah says, 'You shall have no other gods before Me,' and they killed him. They brought the next son and told him to worship the idol. He said the Torah says, 'Whoever sacrifices to other gods shall be destroyed,' and they killed him.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues with the same pattern. Each son refuses with a different פסוק and is killed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The repeated pattern shows each son standing just as firm as the one before. Every brother has his own Torah verse ready.

phrases.english: They brought the next son before the emperor,
and they said to him: Worship the idol!
He said to them: It is written in the Torah:

phrases.aramaic: ״לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ אֱלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים עַל פָּנָי״.
phrases.english: "You shall have no other gods before Me."
phrases.notes: שמות 20:3

phrases.english: They took him out and killed him.
They brought the next son,
and they said to him: Worship the idol!
He said to them: It is written in the Torah:
"Whoever sacrifices to other gods shall be destroyed."
phrases.notes: שמות 22:19

phrases.english: They took him out and killed him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתְיוּהּ לְאִידַּךְ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּקֵיסָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב יהודה's story with the second and third sons
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The second and third sons also refuse, each quoting a פסוק, and are killed.

steps.title: The fourth and fifth sons refuse and are killed
steps.stepSummary: The fourth son quotes 'לא תשתחוה לאל אחר' and the fifth quotes 'שמע ישראל'. Both are killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: They brought the next son and told him to worship the idol. He said the Torah says, 'You shall not bow to another god,' and they killed him. They brought the next son and told him to worship the idol. He said the Torah says, 'Hear, Israel, ה׳ is our God, ה׳ is One,' and they killed him.
steps.whatsHappening: The same pattern repeats for the fourth and fifth sons. The story is still going and will continue with the remaining sons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fifth son quotes שמע ישראל, the basic declaration of belief in one God. Like his brothers, he gives up his life rather than worship an idol.

keyTerms.meaning: Hear, O Israel, the declaration of ה׳'s oneness

phrases.english: They brought the next son,
and they said to him: Worship the idol!
He said to them: It is written in the Torah:
"You shall not bow down to another god."
phrases.notes: שמות 34:14

phrases.english: They took him out and killed him.
They brought the next son,
and they said to him: Worship the idol!
He said to them: It is written in the Torah:
"Hear, Israel: ה׳ is our God, ה׳ is One."
phrases.notes: דברים 6:4

phrases.english: They took him out and killed him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתְיוּהּ לְאִידַּךְ, אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: פְּלַח לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story with the fourth and fifth sons
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fourth and fifth sons also refuse with a פסוק and are killed.

steps.title: The sixth son refuses and is killed
steps.stepSummary: The sixth son is ordered to worship the idol. He refuses by quoting the פסוק that ה׳ is God in heaven and on earth and there is no other. He is killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: They brought the next son and told him to worship the idol. He answered that the תורה says: 'Know today and take to heart that ה׳ is God in heaven above and on earth below; there is no other.' They took him out and killed him.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues with the same pattern as the earlier brothers. The sixth son gives his own פסוק as his reason for refusing, and he is killed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each brother answers with a different פסוק, so each refusal adds a new reason. This son's פסוק says there is no other power anywhere, in heaven or on earth. That means bowing to an idol makes no sense at all.

keyTerms.meaning: They brought the next one (the next brother)
They took him out and killed him

phrases.english: They brought the next one,
they said to him: Worship the idol!
He said to them: It is written in the Torah:
"Know this today and take it to your heart,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי ה׳ הוּא הָאֱלֹהִים בַּשָּׁמַיִם מִמַּעַל
phrases.english: that ה׳ is God in the heavens above
and on the earth below; there is no other."
phrases.notes: דברים 4:39

phrases.english: They took him out and killed him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתְיוּהּ לְאִידַּךְ, אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: פְּלַח לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the pattern of the brothers after the fourth and fifth sons in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sixth son dies rather than worship the idol, because the תורה says there is no other god in heaven or on earth.

steps.title: The seventh son quotes the mutual oath with ה׳
steps.stepSummary: The youngest son is ordered to worship the idol. He quotes the פסוקים of 'you have declared ה׳' and 'ה׳ has declared you.' He explains that ישראל and הקדוש ברוך הוא swore never to exchange each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: They brought the next son and told him to worship the idol. He answered that the תורה says: 'You have declared ה׳... and ה׳ has declared you today.' We already swore to הקדוש ברוך הוא that we will never exchange Him for another god, and He swore to us that He will never exchange us for another nation.
steps.whatsHappening: The seventh son refuses, and he also explains what his פסוק means. The relationship is a two-sided oath: we stay loyal to ה׳, and ה׳ stays loyal to us.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier brothers quoted rules or statements about ה׳. This brother speaks about a relationship, a promise that goes both ways. Worshipping an idol would break our side of a promise that ה׳ keeps on His side.

keyTerms.meaning: You have declared (you chose ה׳ as your God)
He has declared you (ה׳ chose you as His people)

phrases.english: They brought the next one,
they said to him: Worship the idol!
He said to them: It is written in the Torah:
"You have declared ה׳, etc.
phrases.notes: דברים 26:17–18. The word וגו׳ means 'and so on.' He skips ahead to the matching פסוק.

phrases.english: and ה׳ has declared you today."
We already swore to the Holy One, Blessed be He,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין אָנוּ מַעֲבִירִין אוֹתוֹ בְּאֵל אַחֵר,
phrases.english: that we will not exchange Him for another god,
and He too swore to us
that He will not exchange us for another nation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתְיוּהּ לְאִידַּךְ, אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: פְּלַח לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The seventh and last brother faces the same order. He adds an explanation of his פסוק as a two-way oath.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ישראל and הקדוש ברוך הוא are bound by a mutual oath, so ישראל can never exchange ה׳ for an idol.

steps.title: The emperor offers a way out with his ring
steps.stepSummary: קיסר tries to save the youngest boy. He will drop his royal ring, and the boy only needs to bend down and pick it up, so people will think he accepted the king's authority.
steps.simpleTranslation: קיסר said to him: I will throw my royal ring down in front of you. Bend down and pick it up, so that people will say he accepted the king's authority.
steps.whatsHappening: קיסר suggests a trick: the boy does not have to really bow, he only has to look like he is bowing. This step sets up the boy's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new kind of test. It is not a direct order to serve the idol. It is a small act that only looks like giving in. The question is whether something that only looks like surrender is still allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Bend down and pick it up

steps.confusionAlert: קיסר is not asking the boy to worship the idol here. He only asks him to bend down for a ring so it looks like he gave in. The boy refuses even this.

phrases.english: The Caesar said to him:
I will throw down my signet ring in front of you,
phrases.notes: The ring is the king's official seal. Bending to pick it up would look like bowing to the king.

phrases.english: and you bend down and pick it up,
so that people will say:
He has accepted the authority of the king.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ קֵיסָר: אֶישְׁדֵּי לָךְ גּוּשְׁפַּנְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the seventh son refuses outright, קיסר offers him a smaller act that only looks like surrender.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קיסר proposes that the boy only appear to accept the king's authority by picking up the royal ring.

steps.title: The boy refuses with a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The boy says 'woe to you, קיסר.' He argues that if you care this much about your own honor, then God's honor certainly deserves even more care.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Woe to you, קיסר, woe to you, קיסר! If for your own honor it is like this, then for the honor of הקדוש ברוך הוא, how much more so!
steps.whatsHappening: The boy rejects קיסר's offer. He uses קיסר's own reasoning against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קיסר's plan depends on appearances: people seeing the boy bend would count as honoring the king. The boy turns this around with a קל וחומר. If a human king cares so much about how his honor looks, then even looking like he is giving up ה׳'s honor is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Woe to you / what a shame for you
How much more so (the language of a קל וחומר)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that even an act that only looks like surrender to another power is something a Jew must refuse, because ה׳'s honor is greater than any king's.

phrases.english: He said to him: Woe to you, Caesar,
woe to you, Caesar!
For your own honor, this much;
phrases.notes: He means: you care this much that people see others honoring you.

phrases.english: for the honor of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
how much more so!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲבָל עֲלָךְ קֵיסָר, חֲבָל עֲלָךְ קֵיסָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly rejects קיסר's offer from step 24.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole proposal to pick up the ring, even though it is only for appearances.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: קיסר himself cares about appearances of honor. So by a קל וחומר, looking like you are dishonoring הקדוש ברוך הוא is even worse.

steps.title: The mother's last kiss and her message to אברהם
steps.stepSummary: As the youngest is taken to be killed, his mother asks to kiss him. She sends a message to אברהם אבינו: you bound one altar, but I bound seven.
steps.simpleTranslation: As they took him out to kill him, his mother said to them: Give him to me so I can kiss him a little. She said to him: My sons, go and tell your father אברהם: You bound one altar, and I bound seven altars!
steps.whatsHappening: The story turns to the mother. She says goodbye to her last son and compares her sacrifice to אברהם's עקידה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אברהם was ready to give up one son, but in the end יצחק was not killed. She actually gave up all seven sons. Her message shows how great her sacrifice was.

keyTerms.meaning: Let me kiss him a little

phrases.english: They took him out to kill him,
his mother said to them:
Give him to me so I can kiss him a little.
She said to him: My sons,
phrases.notes: Literally 'my sons,' and the next words are plural too. She is talking to him, but her message is for all seven.

phrases.english: go and say to Abraham your father:
You bound one altar,
phrases.notes: This refers to the עקידה, when אברהם bound יצחק on the altar.

phrases.english: but I bound seven altars!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַפְּקוּהּ לְמִיקְטְלֵיהּ, אֲמַרָה לְהוּ אִימֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the youngest son refuses, he is taken to be killed, and his mother speaks.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The mother sees her seven sons as seven offerings, a greater sacrifice than אברהם's single עקידה.

steps.title: The mother dies and a heavenly voice praises her
steps.stepSummary: The mother goes up to the roof, falls, and dies. A בת קול announces: 'The mother of the children is joyful.'
steps.simpleTranslation: She too went up to the roof, fell, and died. A heavenly voice came out and said: 'The mother of the children is joyful.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with the mother's death. Heaven announces that she is a joyful mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בת קול uses a פסוק from תהלים to show that Heaven approved of what she and her sons did. Even though the story is so sad, she is called joyful, because her children died sanctifying ה׳'s name.

keyTerms.meaning: She went up to the roof
The mother of the children is joyful

steps.whatToRemember: This story illustrates the פסוק 'For Your sake we are killed all day.' Each of the seven sons refused עבודה זרה with a different פסוק, the youngest refused even to look like he gave in, and the mother was praised by Heaven as a joyful mother.

phrases.english: She too went up to the roof,
fell, and died.
A heavenly voice came out and said:
"The mother of the children is joyful."
phrases.notes: תהלים 113:9

steps.triggerLanguage: יָצְתָה בַּת קוֹל וְאָמְרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story begun in step 19 with the mother's death and Heaven's verdict.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The woman and her seven sons died for קידוש השם, and Heaven declared her a joyful mother of children.

steps.title: The verse refers to circumcision on the eighth day
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי explains that 'killed for Your sake all day long' refers to מילה, which is done on the eighth day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: This verse is about מילה, which is given on the eighth day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another explanation of the פסוק 'כי עליך הורגנו כל היום.' רבי יהושע בן לוי says it is talking about מילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous lines used the פסוק for the mother and her seven sons, who actually died. רבי יהושע בן לוי reads it in a wider way. Every Jewish family spills the blood of its eight-day-old baby for ה׳'s sake, so in a sense we are 'killed for Him' all the time.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
phrases.notes: He is explaining the same פסוק, 'כי עליך הורגנו כל היום' (תהלים 44:23), that the גמרא used for the 400 children and for the mother and her seven sons.

phrases.english: This is circumcision, which was given for the eighth [day].

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמַר: זוֹ מִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reading of the פסוק that was applied to the mother and seven sons.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Killed for Your sake all day long' refers to מילה on the eighth day.

steps.title: The verse refers to scholars who demonstrate slaughter on themselves
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says the פסוק is about תלמידי חכמים who show the laws of שחיטה using their own bodies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: These are Torah scholars who show the laws of שחיטה on themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives another explanation of the פסוק. It refers to תלמידי חכמים who demonstrate the laws of שחיטה on their own bodies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A teacher who acts out the cut of שחיטה on himself, to show it clearly, puts himself in real danger. These scholars risk being hurt for the sake of teaching Torah, so they too are 'killed for Your sake.'

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
These are Torah scholars
who demonstrate the laws of slaughter on themselves,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אָמַר: אֵלּוּ תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים שֶׁמַּרְאִין הִלְכוֹת שְׁחִיטָה בְּעַצְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fourth reading of the same פסוק, after the 400 children, the mother and seven sons, and רבי יהושע בן לוי's reading about מילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק refers to scholars who risk injury by demonstrating שחיטה on themselves.

steps.title: רבא: demonstrate anything on yourself except slaughter
steps.stepSummary: רבא's teaching supports ריש לקיש. You may act out anything on yourself except שחיטה and one other matter, which shows that demonstrating שחיטה on yourself is dangerous.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבא said: A person may demonstrate any matter on himself, except for שחיטה and 'another thing.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching of רבא to support ריש לקיש's explanation. רבא warns against demonstrating שחיטה on yourself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's warning shows that acting out שחיטה on your own body is truly dangerous. That backs up ריש לקיש: the scholars who do it anyway are risking themselves for Torah teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: A person may show (demonstrate) on himself
'Another thing,' a polite way of referring to something not said openly

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying it is fine to demonstrate שחיטה. He says the opposite: everything may be demonstrated on yourself EXCEPT שחיטה. That is exactly why the scholars who do it are in danger.

phrases.english: As Rava said:
A person may demonstrate any matter on himself,
except for slaughter and "another thing."
phrases.notes: 'Another thing' is a polite way of referring to marital relations.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רָבָא: כֹּל מִילֵּי לִיחְזֵי אִינִישׁ בְּנַפְשֵׁיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports ריש לקיש's reading by showing that demonstrating שחיטה on oneself is dangerous.
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's claim that scholars who demonstrate שחיטה on themselves are 'killed for Your sake.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's rule that one may demonstrate anything on oneself except שחיטה and 'another thing.'

steps.title: The verse refers to scholars who 'kill themselves' over Torah
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says the פסוק is about תלמידי חכמים who wear themselves out completely for Torah study, following a teaching of ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: These are Torah scholars who kill themselves over words of Torah, in line with ריש לקיש.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives yet another explanation of the פסוק. It is about scholars who give up everything, even their comfort and health, to learn Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'killed' does not mean actual death or physical danger. It means devoting your whole life to learning. רב נחמן bases this on a teaching of ריש לקיש, which the גמרא quotes next.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Kill themselves,' meaning they give themselves over completely
In line with, following the view of

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
These are Torah scholars who kill themselves
over words of Torah,
in line with Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish –

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: אֵלּוּ תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים שֶׁמְּמִיתִין עַצְמָן עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fifth reading of the same פסוק, after the 400 children, the mother and seven sons, מילה, and scholars who demonstrate שחיטה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק refers to scholars who devote themselves totally to Torah study.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: Torah lasts only in one who 'dies' for it
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש teaches, from the פסוק 'זאת התורה אדם כי ימות באהל,' that Torah stays only with someone who gives himself over completely to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As ריש לקיש said: Words of Torah last only in someone who kills himself over them, as it says: 'This is the Torah: a man, when he dies in a tent.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the teaching of ריש לקיש that רב נחמן בר יצחק relied on. It is the source for his explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש reads 'This is the Torah: a man who dies in a tent' as a hint that Torah is gained by someone who 'dies' in the tent of learning. That supports רב נחמן: such scholars are 'killed for Your sake all day long.'
steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא gives five ways to read 'killed for Your sake all day long': the 400 captive children who drowned themselves, the mother and seven sons, מילה, scholars who demonstrate שחיטה on themselves, and scholars who give themselves over completely to Torah.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
Words of Torah do not endure
except in one who kills himself over them,
as it is said:

phrases.aramaic: ״זֹאת הַתּוֹרָה אָדָם כִּי יָמוּת בְּאֹהֶל וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: "This is the Torah: a man when he dies in a tent, etc."
phrases.notes: במדבר 19:14. ריש לקיש reads it as: the Torah belongs to the one who 'dies' in the tent of learning.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ: אֵין דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה מִתְקַיְּימִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the source that רב נחמן בר יצחק relied on.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן בר יצחק's reading that the פסוק refers to scholars who 'kill themselves' over Torah.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ריש לקיש's teaching from במדבר 19:14 that Torah stays only with one who 'dies' over it.

steps.title: רבה בר בר חנה begins a new statement about forty סאה
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה starts a new teaching in the name of רבי יוחנן, opening with 'forty סאה.' The rest of the statement continues past this section.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Forty סאה...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is moving to a new teaching. Only the first words appear here, so this line sets up what comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new statement, not another reading of the פסוק. We only see the opening, a large measure ('forty סאה'). What that measure refers to is explained in the next lines.

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Forty se'a
phrases.notes: His sentence isn't finished yet. It keeps going in the next lines.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of the פסוק and opens a new teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opening of a statement by רבי יוחנן about 'forty סאה,' which continues in the next lines.
